description:
Format-preserving placeholders, their use through field rules, and the observed value types. Shared vectors: the Python SDK is the source of truth and any other SDK runs the same file and must reproduce every expected value exactly. Each case is {name, op, input, expected}; op names one of the operations below. JSON bodies are source text, masked bodies are Python json.dumps text, and form and query output is urlencode(doseq=True) text; compare them as strings. A string of many equal characters is written {"$repeat": "a", "times": 65537}, and a string made of such parts {"$concat": [...]}; expand them before use.
Operations used in this file:
- placeholder: input {semantic_type, values, salt, email_domain}; values are typed scalars {type: str|int|float|bool|none, value or text}, with text the Python repr of a float and the decimal digits of an int; the key is the salt string as UTF-8 truncated to 64 bytes (null or empty means no key). Each value is generated twice and the two results must be equal. expected {salt_key_hex, outputs} with typed outputs.
- apply_field_rules: input {field_rules, body, headers, query, content_type, project_defaults, salt, email_domain}; compile the field rules, then mask a request. project_defaults is null or {field_masks, regex_masks}, compiled as the project's extra rules. salt is the STUBSMITH_MASK_SALT string (null means unset). email_domain null means the default. expected {body, headers, query}, compared as exact text.
- apply_resp_field_rules: same input as apply_field_rules without query, plus resp_status (an integer or null); expected {body, headers}.
- compile_field_rules: input {field_rules}; expected the compiled sets as sorted lists: keep_body, keep_query, keep_header, keep_resp, keep_resp_header, keep_resp_status, mask_resp_status, keep_resp_header_status, mask_resp_header_status (the last four as [status, path] pairs sorted by status then path), and the objects body_mask_types, query_mask_types, resp_mask_types.
- classify_scalar: input {json}: JSON source text of one value, parsed as Python json.loads does; expected {label} (null for no label).
- extract_value_types: input {body, content_type}; expected {value_types}.
